## Taken from Makie  - we improved performance and simplified the implementation for our use case
function streamplot_impl(CallType, f, limits::Rect{N, T}, resolutionND, stepsize, maxsteps = 500, dens = 1.0, color_func = norm) where {N, T}
    resolution = to_ndim(Vec{N, Int}, resolutionND, last(resolutionND))
    mask = trues(resolution...) # unvisited squares
    line_points = Point{N, Float32}[]
    _cfunc = x -> to_color(color_func(x))
    ColorType = typeof(_cfunc(Point{N, Float32}(0.0)))
    line_colors = ColorType[]
    dt = Point{N, Float32}(stepsize)
    mini, maxi = minimum(limits), maximum(limits)
    r = ntuple(N) do i
        LinRange(mini[i], maxi[i], resolution[i] + 1)
    end
    rv = collect.(r)
    apply_f(x0, P) = P <: Point ? f(x0) : f(x0...)

    # see http://extremelearning.com.au/unreasonable-effectiveness-of-quasirandom-sequences/
    ϕ = (MathConstants.φ, 1.324717957244746, 1.2207440846057596)[N]
    acoeff = ϕ .^ (-(1:N))
    n_points = 0 # count visited squares
    ind = 0 # index of low discrepancy sequence
    while n_points < prod(resolution) * min(one(dens), dens) # fill up to 100*dens% of mask
        # next index from low discrepancy sequence
        lolind = ind
        tup = ntuple(N) do i
            j = ceil(Int, ((0.5 + acoeff[i] * lolind) % 1) * resolution[i])
            clamp(j, 1, size(mask, i))::Int64
        end
        c = CartesianIndex(tup)
        ind += 1
        if mask[c]
            x0 = Point{N, Float32}(
                ntuple(N) do i
                    first(r[i]) + (c[i] - 0.5) * step(r[i])
                end
            )
            point = apply_f(x0, CallType)
            if !(point isa Point2 || point isa Point3)
                error("Function passed to streamplot must return Point2 or Point3")
            end
            pnorm = norm(point)
            color = _cfunc(point)
            mask[c] = false
            n_points += 1
            for d in (-1, 1)
                n_linepoints = 1
                x = x0
                ccur = c
                push!(line_points, Point{N, Float32}(NaN), x)
                push!(line_colors, color, color)
                while x in limits && n_linepoints < maxsteps
                    point = apply_f(x, CallType)
                    pnorm = norm(point)
                    x = x .+ d .* dt .* point ./ pnorm
                    if !(x in limits)
                        break
                    end
                    # WHAT? Why does point behave different from tuple in this
                    indices = map(r, Tuple(x)) do ri, xi
                        searchsortedlast(ri, xi)
                    end
                    idx = CartesianIndex(indices)
                    if idx != ccur && checkbounds(Bool, mask, idx)
                        if !mask[idx]
                            break
                        end
                        mask[idx] = false
                        n_points += 1
                        ccur = idx
                    end
                    push!(line_points, x)
                    push!(line_colors, _cfunc(point))
                    n_linepoints += 1
                end
            end
        end
    end

    return (
        line_points,
        line_colors,
    )
end

@inline function search_range(range::AbstractRange, value)
    # For LinRange, we can calculate the index directly
    idx = (value - first(range)) / step(range) + 1
    return clamp(unsafe_trunc(Int, floor(idx)), 1, length(range))
end

# Simple linear interpolation function
@inbounds function interpolated_getindex(data_3d, ranges, x, y, z)
    x_range, y_range, z_range = ranges

    # Map coordinates to grid indices
    xi = (x - first(x_range)) / step(x_range) + 1.0
    yi = (y - first(y_range)) / step(y_range) + 1.0
    zi = (z - first(z_range)) / step(z_range) + 1.0

    # Clamp to valid bounds
    xi = clamp(xi, 1, size(data_3d, 1))
    yi = clamp(yi, 1, size(data_3d, 2))
    zi = clamp(zi, 1, size(data_3d, 3))

    # Get integer and fractional parts
    xf = floor(xi)
    yf = floor(yi)
    zf = floor(zi)
    x_idx = unsafe_trunc(Int, xf)
    y_idx = unsafe_trunc(Int, yf)
    z_idx = unsafe_trunc(Int, zf)
    x_frac = xi - xf
    y_frac = yi - yf
    z_frac = zi - zf
    # Ensure we don't go out of bounds
    x_idx = clamp(x_idx, 1, size(data_3d, 1) - 1)
    y_idx = clamp(y_idx, 1, size(data_3d, 2) - 1)
    z_idx = clamp(z_idx, 1, size(data_3d, 3) - 1)

    # Trilinear interpolation
    c000 = data_3d[x_idx, y_idx, z_idx]
    c100 = data_3d[x_idx+1, y_idx, z_idx]
    c010 = data_3d[x_idx, y_idx+1, z_idx]
    c110 = data_3d[x_idx+1, y_idx+1, z_idx]
    c001 = data_3d[x_idx, y_idx, z_idx+1]
    c101 = data_3d[x_idx+1, y_idx, z_idx+1]
    c011 = data_3d[x_idx, y_idx+1, z_idx+1]
    c111 = data_3d[x_idx+1, y_idx+1, z_idx+1]

    # Interpolate along x
    c00 = c000 * (1.0 - x_frac) + c100 * x_frac
    c01 = c001 * (1.0 - x_frac) + c101 * x_frac
    c10 = c010 * (1.0 - x_frac) + c110 * x_frac
    c11 = c011 * (1.0 - x_frac) + c111 * x_frac

    # Interpolate along y
    c0 = c00 * (1.0 - y_frac) + c10 * y_frac
    c1 = c01 * (.01 - y_frac) + c11 * y_frac

    # Interpolate along z
    return c0 * (1.0 - z_frac) + c1 * z_frac
end

function velocity_to_lines(vf::VelocityField)
    # Extract x, y, z components from xyz
    x = [p[1] for p in vf.xyz]
    y = [p[2] for p in vf.xyz]
    z = [p[3] for p in vf.xyz]

    # Extract velocity components from u
    ux = [v[1] for v in vf.u]
    uy = [v[2] for v in vf.u]
    uz = [v[3] for v in vf.u]

    # Extract grid dimensions
    nx, ny, nz = vf.n[1], vf.n[2], vf.n[3]

    # Reconstruct 3D arrays for velocity components
    ux_3d = reshape(ux, nx, ny, nz)
    uy_3d = reshape(uy, nx, ny, nz)
    uz_3d = reshape(uz, nx, ny, nz)

    # Get unique sorted grid points for each axis
    x_grid = sort(unique(x))
    y_grid = sort(unique(y))
    z_grid = sort(unique(z))

    # Convert to LinRange for Interpolations.jl scaling
    x_range = LinRange(x_grid[1], x_grid[end], length(x_grid))
    y_range = LinRange(y_grid[1], y_grid[end], length(y_grid))
    z_range = LinRange(z_grid[1], z_grid[end], length(z_grid))

    # Create a function to interpolate the velocity field at a given point
    # and return all three velocity components: u = (ux, uy, uz)
    function interpolated_vector_field(point)
        x, y, z = Float64.(point)
        return Point3f(
            interpolated_getindex(ux_3d, (x_range, y_range, z_range), x, y, z),
            interpolated_getindex(uy_3d, (x_range, y_range, z_range), x, y, z),
            interpolated_getindex(uz_3d, (x_range, y_range, z_range), x, y, z)
        )
    end

    # Get the streamline density from the UI settings
    streamline_density = vf.ui_states.streamline_settings

    # Create a streamplot with the interpolated vector field

    minimaxi = extrema.((x, y, z))
    mini = Vec3f(first.(minimaxi))
    maxi = Vec3f(last.(minimaxi))
    limits = Rect3f(mini, maxi .- mini)
    return streamplot_impl(Point, interpolated_vector_field, limits, (32, 32, 32), 0.01, 20, streamline_density, norm)
end

"""
    handle_recenter_button_click(scene::Scene)

Handle the recenter button click by updating the camera to the default position.

# Arguments
- `scene::Scene`: The scene to update

# Returns
- `Nothing`: The scene is updated in place
"""
function handle_recenter_button_click(scene::Scene)
    cam = cameracontrols(scene)
    eye = Vec3f(2.5, 2.5, 2.5)
    lookat = Vec3f(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
    up = Vec3f(0, 0, 1)  # Z-up orientation
    update_cam!(scene, cam, eye, lookat, up)
end

######################## MAIN GUI FUNCTION #####################################

function calculate_streamlines(time_val, base_flow_val, eigen_str, streamline_density_val, velocity_field)
     # Convert time value to index for internal processing
    time_index = findfirst(x -> x == time_val, velocity_field.time_steps)
    # Get eigenstate components from textbox
    if eigen_str === nothing || eigen_str == ""
        eigen_str = "1"
    end

    # Create a new settings object with current values
    new_settings = PlotSettings(time_index, eigen_str, base_flow_val, streamline_density_val)
    # Create a new VelocityField with the updated settings
    field = DataManager.calculate_velocity_field(update_velocity_field(velocity_field, new_settings))
    # Calculate the velocity field and update the plot
    return velocity_to_lines(field)
end


"""
    run_gui()

Launch the visualization GUI with a 3D plotter on the right (2/3) and
controls panel on the left (1/3).

# Arguments
- `None`: No arguments are required

# Returns
- `Figure`: The figure object
"""
function run_gui(data_dir; size_x=1800, size_y=1080)
    #Initialize variable to hold a reference to
    # a velocity field object
    velocity_field = load_data(data_dir)

    # Create the figure with appropriate size
    f = Figure(size=(size_x, size_y), figure_padding=(0, 0, 0, 0), backgroundcolor = (0.322, 0.341, 0.431), fontsize = 20)

    # Create a control panel that will properly resize with the window
    control_panel = f[1, 1] = GridLayout(tellheight = false, tellwidth = false, alignmode = Outside(30,30,0,0))

    # Make the right column an LScene for the 3D plot
    plot_right = LScene(f[1, 2], show_axis=false)
    plot_right.tellwidth = false
    plot_right.tellheight = false

    # Set up the grid layout with fixed column proportions AFTER creating both columns
    left_column_size = 1/3
    right_column_size = 2/3
    colsize!(f.layout, 1, Relative(left_column_size))
    colsize!(f.layout, 2, Relative(right_column_size))

    # Background panel for the control area that will resize with the window
    background_panel = Box(f[1, 1], color = RGBf(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), strokewidth = 0)
    background_panel.tellwidth = false
    background_panel.tellheight = false

    # Add spacing between elements
    # Create a nested layout for the controls to ensure proper relative positioning
    controls = GridLayout(tellheight = false, tellwidth = true, valign=:top)
    control_panel[1, 1] = controls

    # Position controls with proper resizing behavior
    # Top controls - leave some space at top
    status_label = Label(controls[1, 1:2], "Data Loaded", fontsize=20)
    status_label.halign = :center
    il = 2

    # Middle controls

    time_values = velocity_field.time_steps
    time_step_slider = SliderGrid(controls[il, 1:2],
        (label="Time (s)", range=time_values, startvalue=time_values[1]))

    # Set slider font size and make it resize properly
    for i in 1:length(time_step_slider.sliders)
        time_step_slider.labels[i].fontsize = 20
        time_step_slider.sliders[i].width = Relative(0.8)
        time_step_slider.sliders[i].halign = :center
    end

    # # Add empty space
    # Eigenstate field
    eigenstate_label = Label(controls[il+1, 1], "Flow Structure \nComponents", fontsize=20, halign = :left)
    eigenstate_textbox = Textbox(controls[il+1, 2], fontsize=20, placeholder = "Total",
                        boxcolor = :white, boxcolor_hover = :white, boxcolor_focused = :white,
                        textcolor_placeholder = :black, halign = :left)
    eigenstate_textbox.width = Relative(0.8)

    # Streamline Density
    streamline_density_label = Label(controls[il+2, 1], "Streamline Density", fontsize=20, halign = :left)
    streamline_density_textbox = Textbox(controls[il+2, 2], fontsize=20,
                        boxcolor = :white, boxcolor_hover = :white, boxcolor_focused = :white,
                        textcolor_placeholder = :black, halign = :left)
    streamline_density_textbox.width = Relative(0.5)
    streamline_density_textbox.displayed_string = "1"  # Default value

    # Base Flow Checkbox
    base_flow_label = Label(controls[il+3, 1], "Base Flow", fontsize=20)
    base_flow_checkbox = Checkbox(controls[il+3, 2], checked=true, tellwidth=false, tellheight=false, size = 20, halign = :left)


    # Bottom buttons - use higher row numbers to push them down
    recenter_button = Button(controls[il+4, 1:2], label="Recenter", fontsize=20)
    recenter_button.width = Relative(0.8)
    recenter_button.height = 40
    recenter_button.halign = :center

    update_plot_button = Button(controls[il+5, 1:2], label="Update Plot", fontsize=20)
    update_plot_button.width = Relative(0.8)
    update_plot_button.height = 40
    update_plot_button.halign = :center

    # # Add empty space

    ############ UI FUNCTIONALITY ###########################################
    # Connects the UI elements to their functionality as
    # defined by the helper functions defined above

    # Stretch out the UI
    rowsize!(controls, 1, 100)
    rowsize!(controls, 2, 100)
    rowsize!(controls, 5, 100)


    # Set up the recenter button functionality
    scene = plot_right.scene
    on(recenter_button.clicks) do _
        handle_recenter_button_click(scene)
    end
    t_obs = time_step_slider.sliders[1].value
    bfc_obs = base_flow_checkbox.checked
    density_string = streamline_density_textbox.displayed_string
    density = Observable(1.0)
    on(density_string; update=true) do string
        number = tryparse(Float64, string)
        if !isnothing(number)
            if number >= 0 && number <= 1
                density[] = number
            else
                @warn("Error: Streamline density must be between 0 and 1")
            end
        else
            @warn("Error: Streamline density must be a valid number. Found: $string")
        end
    end

    lineppoints = Observable((Point3f[], Float32[]))

    # Use onany_latest to discard intermediate updates and only process the latest
    Makie.onany_latest(t_obs, bfc_obs, density, update=true) do time_val, base_flow_val, density
        lineppoints[] = calculate_streamlines(
            time_val, base_flow_val,
            eigenstate_textbox.displayed_string[],
            density,
            velocity_field
        )
        return
    end

    # Reference to the streamplot object
    # Add a colorbar to the plot

    min_point = Point3f(-0.05, -0.05, -0.05)
    max_point = Point3f(1.05, 1.05, 1.05)
    box = Rect3f(min_point, max_point - min_point)
    wireframe!(plot_right, box, color = :gray, linewidth = 0.5)
    lineplot = lines!(plot_right, map(first, lineppoints), color=map(last, lineppoints), colorrange=(0, 21))
    cb = Colorbar(f[1, 2], lineplot, ticklabelsize = 16, minorticksvisible = true,
                width = 30, height = Relative(0.65), halign = 0.95)
    return f
end

end # module ReynKoWebViz
